item.title: Assembly Drill 2026-11-16: reverse-function
item.description:
Target: Windows x86-64 (arg in `ecx`, return in `eax`).
Reverse this short function to equivalent C:
```asm mystery: lea eax, [rcx+15] and eax, -16 ret ```
What does it return for 0, 1, 16, 17 and 40?
---
## Answer
```c unsigned mystery(unsigned x) { return (x + 15) & ~15u; // round x up to a multiple of 16 } ```
Results: 0, 16, 16, 32, 48.
## Explanation
- `lea eax, [rcx+15]` just computes x+15 into eax; nothing is read from memory. - `-16` is 0xFFFFFFF0 in two's complement, the same as `~15`: all bits set except the low 4. ANDing with it clears those 4 bits, rounding down to a multiple of 16. - Adding 15 first turns "round down" into "round up": exact multiples stay put, anything else moves to the next one. Allocators and stack setup use this align-up idiom constantly.
